items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I replaced Sid Catlett in Boston to play George Wein's Storyville.

ctx.x: He's one of the great young ones, don't you think?

Yes, because at the particular time when Sid Catlett and I - I replaced Sid Catlett in Boston to play George Wein's Storyville. When we looked at Aldan - 'cause we always tried to find a replacement for us, all throughout the United States. As you know, you had a little cousin that I tried to do something. He played with Lester Young. O.K.?

items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And I brought all the guys from the big band, the Harry Edisons, Buck Claytons, everybody. Jo Jones. And Eubie Blake. I brought everybody.

ctx.x: Multiple stages, simultaneously. A logistics nightmare I can only imagine. And I think, correct me if I'm wrong here, you were also somehow kind of got involved in booking beyond the Festival, which served some benefit to you in getting guys over to Nice in the first place.

It's funny about life, because what I'm doing now is totally different from what I did at Nice. Because in Europe, at that time, there were a lot of avant garde festivals happening. Nobody was paying attention to traditional jazz. And I said, "I'm going to bring all the great players over, 'cause they were all still alive: Earl Hines, Teddy Wilson." Nobody cared about them anymore. They were all into either (post?), Coltrane was already big by 74, and you had these festivals in Germany, and you'd read the papers…
Did you ever make money in Nice?
